messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SLO alert: streaming-inference p99 > 5s for the last 5m on route /v1/stream (gpu-dedicated-3). Auto-page triggered (priority: paged).

Maya (oncall): Acked. I see the alert. Pulling dashboards and recent deploys. @Ashwin can you sanity-check model and runtime changes?

Ashwin (runtime): Looking now. p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~1.1s over last 10m. p99 spikes 5–8s. Trace correlation shows tail events from the continuous-batching execution path (cont-batch) on streaming requests — mixed sequence lengths causing some batches to wait.

Zr (SRE): Noted. Runbook reference: <https://redwood/runbooks/latency-triage>. Can you paste the exact trace ids? I want to check if this is scheduling-fairness related or a kernel/blocking issue.

Ashwin (runtime): Sample traces: `trace/9a1b2c..`, `trace/9a1b2d..` — both show long sequences (tokens > 12k) holding KV cache and blocking batch flushes. There's a scheduling fairness change we shipped in last deploy that weights batch assembly differently. Might be interacting badly with streaming prefix caching.

Dave (infra): We did flip a fairness flag in the scheduler earlier today (deploy 2026-03-14T09:10Z). If this is the regression, we can either roll that back or disable cont-batch on streaming routes temporarily. Rolling back scheduler-wide has risk; prefer targeted mitigation first.

Maya (oncall): Agreed. Start targeted mitigations: 1) route streaming requests on gpu-dedicated-3 to legacy batching path (disable cont-batch) 2) cap max batch size for streaming route to 8 3) enable per-route short-seq priority for batches. I'll trigger env overrides.

Maya (oncall): Command I'm about to run (deploy-bot):
```
/deploy setenv streaming-service --pool gpu-dedicated-3 CONT_BATCH_ENABLED=false CONT_BATCH_MAX_SIZE=8
```

incident-bot: Deploy job started: deploy/streaming-service@release-2026-03-14-0930. 16 instances in pool gpu-dedicated-3 will be updated.

Dave (infra): Rolling update in progress. 4/16 done -> 25%. Will watch kernel metrics and GPU utilization.

Ingrid (support): Ping — which customers are impacted? I have a case from FinAlpha about streaming stalls.

Samira (prod-eng): FinAlpha had ~3% of sessions with stalls around 6s. Their sessions are long (interactive transcripts). We should message them with a short note: "We're investigating increased streaming latency and applying a targeted mitigation; we'll keep you updated." Ingrid can you draft an update?

Ingrid (support): Drafting now. Will send to FinAlpha contacts and include workaround note (they can reduce max_chunk_size client-side for now).

Ashwin (runtime): After the first few instances flipped to legacy path, p99 on /v1/stream dropped to ~320ms for typical sessions. However long-seq p99 still around ~1.2s for sequences > 16k until all hosts are updated.

Maya (oncall): Good. Status: mitigation deployed to 50% of pool (8/16). Metrics: p95 back to ~140ms, p99 aggregated down from 6–8s to 400ms. No errors introduced.

Zr (SRE): Can we confirm the root cause hypothesis? If cont-batch scheduling fairness allows a long sequence to hold a batch window open, short requests behind it experience tail latency. We need either fairness fix or cap on batch assembly TTL for streaming.

Ashwin (runtime): Agree. Evidence: batch assembly times spike when a long seq is present; logs show `assemble_loop.wait_ms` hitting TTL window. Proposed next steps: 1) quick fix: cap assembly TTL for streaming requests to 15ms OR cap max batch size 8 (we applied cap). 2) mid-term: change scheduler to not let single long-seq hold headroom — add weight decay for sequences > N tokens. 3) long-term: introduce per-route batching profiles and isolation for mixed-sequence workloads. I'll file a follow-up PR.

Maya (oncall): Filing an incident follow-up ticket now and assigning to Ashwin + Dave for the scheduler change. Immediate mitigation stable; I'll continue to watch for 15m.

Maya (oncall): Incident slack note for ops log: `mitigation=cont-batch disabled on streaming route; CONT_BATCH_MAX_SIZE=8 applied to pool gpu-dedicated-3; observed p99 drop from ~6-8s -> ~400ms aggregated`

incident-bot: Deploy job succeeded: deploy/streaming-service@release-2026-03-14-0930 -> all 16 instances updated.

Dave (infra): Full pool now on legacy path. GPU utilization slight increase due to less optimal batching, but within capacity. Monitoring for cost delta.

Ashwin (runtime): After full mitigation, p99 for streaming global now ~360ms, p95 ~130ms. Remaining tails only for sessions with extremely long sequences and they are now rare. I'll open PR for scheduler-weight-decay (ENG-RUNTIME-4321) and include a regression test in our perf harness.

Samira (prod-eng): Action items / owners: Ashwin -> runtime change (ENG-RUNTIME-4321). Dave -> evaluate cost impact and roll plan. Maya -> incident report and customer comms. Ingrid -> send FinAlpha update.

Maya (oncall): Handoff to next oncall in 30m: I'll leave monitoring hooks and runbook notes in the incident ticket. If anything regresses, escalate to oncall-senior.

Ingrid (support): Sent update to FinAlpha: short note + expected timeline. They replied: "thx for the quick fix, will monitor" :thumbsup:

Maya (oncall): Wrapping up here. Root cause likely cont-batch scheduler fairness interacting with mixed sequence lengths on streaming route. Mitigation applied and stable. Follow-ups created. Moving to post-incident review.

Zr (SRE): Adding this to the weekly postmortem board. Recommend we add load tests with mixed sequence-length distribution to catch this earlier.

Maya (oncall): End of thread — handing off.
